text:
Lena: Quick heads-up from canary: warmup gets stuck on a few gzipped safetensors bundles. Not OOMs, but repeated small-range 206s and checksum failures.
storage-bot: [alert] warmup-read-error model=image-gen-2 shard=shard-9 event=checksum_mismatch
Omar: Can you paste the minimal repro logs?
Lena: sure, sample: 
```
2026-04-02T11:22:10Z range fetch 0-65535 -> 206
2026-04-02T11:22:10Z verify_after_decompress expected=0f1e2d got=000000
2026-04-02T11:22:11Z retrying range backoff=30ms
```
Ravi: Looks like the decompressor is fed a truncated gz stream because the range cut through the gzip header. We verify after decompressing today.
Omar: Two immediate paths: (A) conservative priming: increase initial range window to capture full gzip header (e.g., 200KB) or (B) manifest-aware verify: include compressed_digest so loader can check compressed bytes before decompress.
Lena: I tried (A) on a small canary and stalls dropped from 7->1 but bytes transferred up ~2x for tiny shards.
Ravi: I like a hybrid: elastic priming. Keep small initial read; on the first checksum mismatch, perform a single elastic prime (e.g., 512KB) and reverify. Only fall back to fetching the whole compressed object if that fails.
Omar: Good compromise. Also we should add an explicit manifest field: compression.type = "gzip" and compression.digest_sha256 optional. If present loader verifies compressed bytes first and skips elastic prime.
Lena: Metrics proposal: loader.gz_checksum_mismatch, loader.gz_elastic_primes, loader.gz_compressed_verify_fail. Tag with model, shard, region, canary.
Ravi: API boundary note: loader should still present decompressed safetensors to runtime, but expose meta: compression.type and compression.digest if available so ops can be audited. Transport layer should provide raw byte ranges for checksum verification.
Omar: Tests: unit for partial-gzip headers, integration via a stub HTTP server that returns split gz ranges, and an end-to-end canary with synthetic gzipped bundles. Add a stress test hitting CDNs since re-chunking can alter ranges.
Lena: Long-term: sidecar index file at publish-time with per-compressed-chunk checksums. That would let us validate small ranges without elastic priming. Needs publisher tool changes and compatibility story.
Ravi: Action items: Omar -> loader: elastic priming + compressed-verify path + telemetry. Lena -> create manifest schema PR and example bundles. Elaine (storage) -> update publishing docs and CDN guidance. I'll add unit tests for partial-gzip decompression.
storage-bot: ticket INF-9001 created: "elastic-gzip-priming + compressed digest + sidecar-index RFC" assigned eng-ml.
Lena: I'll open the RFC-followup issue and include rollout checklist and metrics dashboard links. Ping me if canary spikes reappear. :rocket:
